The RES-aware calibration framework operates by adjusting model confidence in response to observed outcomes, leveraging online convex optimization to iteratively refine probability estimates. The core duality lies between minimizing Brier score and maximizing resolution under reliability constraints. When a model is underconfident—its predicted probabilities cluster near 0.5—the system can increase calibrated variance (RES) to better reflect true posterior sharpness. This requires outcome-fitted expansion under a REL guard to prevent overfitting or free-stretching. The calibrated identity BS = UNC − Var[P] establishes a direct link between uncertainty, variance, and forecast quality. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian inference with conformal validity; in GSE, it enables adaptive decision-making through OGD-driven state transitions. Failure modes include REL violation, non-convex loss landscapes, and insufficient data for reliable updates.
